options.text: A search warrant had been brought when the police raided his house.

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Most of voters in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Most of voters' i.e. error lies in this part of the sentence.**

***__Key Points__**

**In the given sentence, **the usage of **'Most of voters'** is incorrect instead use **'Most voters'**

__
 
• **According to grammar,** '**Most' is a determiner** which is used for the nouns to determine them as it is determiner hence it has no effect on the verb. 
 
• If we read further the verb of the sentence is 'seem' which is a plural verb. So the subject of the sentence should be a plural noun which is going to be 'Voters'

**So the correct sentence is-** ***Most voters** in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__***

 
• **'Most of' is also a quantifier** and the structure is Most of + definite article + noun. In this case, the verb should be according to the noun.*
 
• *Let's see an example-*
 
 
• *​***Most of the houses** in the capital don't **have** piped water. 
 
 
 
• **So the given sentence can also be corrected in the other way also-** *Most of the voters in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.*
